data.name: Franjo
data.gender_notes: Franjo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Frankish name ‘Frank’, meaning 'free man'. This name was adopted by the early Christians, becoming a popular given name throughout Europe. The name Franjo carries the meaning “Free, frank” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Franjo usually hope their child will grow to embody free, frank and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Franjo belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Free, frank.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Franjo total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

The name became closely associated with the spread of Christianity throughout Europe, inspiring many to embrace a new faith and a new way of life.

historical_references.reference: Francisco de Borja (1510-1572) was a Spanish Roman Catholic cardinal and a member of the Society of Jesus. He is best known for his role as the founder of the Society of Mary, a religious order for women.
historical_references.context: Francisco de Borja, also known as St. Francis Borgia, was a prominent figure in the Counter-Reformation. He dedicated his life to religious and charitable works, and his establishment of the Society of Mary helped to strengthen the Catholic Church in Spain.
